clue.text: Generous applause only a few get

parts.note: a hand is a round of applause, as in 'give them a big hand'
some means a limited number, only a few

explanation.surface: A warm ovation is something only a lucky handful of performers ever receive.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Generous' looks like an adjective for the applause, but it is the definition, in the sense of a handsome (large, liberal) gift.
explanation.definitionFit: A handsome sum or offer is a liberal, large one, so the word can mean bountiful.

clue.text: Set to become ruthless

explanation.surface: Someone is poised to turn hard-hearted.
explanation.definitionFit: Concrete or jelly that sets grows firm; a person who grows callous and pitiless has hardened their heart.

clue.text: A quarter scoffed, being tidy

parts.note: a quarter of the compass is one of its four points, here N for north
to scoff food is to eat it greedily

explanation.surface: Someone wolfed down a quarter of something while keeping things neat.
explanation.definitionFit: To tidy is to put in order and make neat, a verb sense.

clue.text: Projector with an arm-rest

explanation.surface: A device for throwing things that comes with somewhere to lean your arm.
explanation.definitionFit: A slingshot hurls stones, a projector of missiles; a cloth support hung from the neck cradles an injured arm.

clue.text: Streams forms for schoolteachers

indicators.note: forms as a verb means shapes or makes up, so the letters of streams are reshaped

explanation.surface: Schools split pupils into streams and forms, grouped for their teachers.
explanation.walkthrough: Streams and forms both look like school groupings, but 'forms' is the anagram signal acting on STREAMS.
explanation.definitionFit: In British schools male teachers were traditionally called masters.

clue.text: Father exercised, but took a breather

parts.note: pa is an informal word for a father
to exercise a right or skill is to use it

explanation.surface: Dad worked out, then stopped for a rest.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Exercised' suggests a workout, but here it means put to use.
explanation.definitionFit: To take a breather is to stop briefly and rest, the same as halting for a moment.

clue.text: A German article about an outfit's director

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so the article goes around the outfit

parts.note: der is the masculine form of 'the' in German
a dress is an outfit; the 's is not a letter

explanation.surface: A German article written about a fashion outfit's creative director.
explanation.walkthrough: The 'director' here is someone who directs, as one addresses a letter or a speech, not a film boss.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who directs words or a letter to a person is the one sending it, so a director in that sense.

clue.text: inform on other criminals repeatedly in prison

indicators.note: repeatedly says the word is given twice in a row

parts.note: to sing is slang for confessing and grassing on accomplices

explanation.surface: A convict keeps snitching on fellow inmates while locked up.
explanation.walkthrough: Sing Sing is a famous maximum-security prison in New York State.
explanation.definitionFit: This is the proper name of a well-known New York correctional facility.

clue.text: One's maybe served outside, so cut off

indicators.note: outside says the rearranged letters sit around the other piece
maybe hints the word served could be arranged another way

parts.note: one's is read as I'S, Roman one plus is

explanation.surface: A tennis player's serve lands out, so the point is lost.
explanation.walkthrough: 'One's' must be read as I (Roman one) plus 's, not as a possessive; 'maybe' signals the rearrangement and 'outside' the wrapping. The tennis surface hides it all.
explanation.definitionFit: To sever completely, to separate or divide, is an old verb with this exact sense.

clue.text: Most enthusiastic about a new diet's composition

parts.note: re means about or concerning, as in letters

indicators.note: composition means putting together, so the letters of a and the reworked diet are made up afresh
new signals the letters of diet's take a fresh order

explanation.surface: The keenest dieter talks about how a new eating plan is put together.
explanation.walkthrough: Two rearrangement signals: 'new' works on diet's (the 's counted as S) and 'composition' on A plus that, all after RE. RE for 'about' is the usual crossword sense, as in business letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Being the most prepared and willing, the keenest, is the superlative of eager readiness.

clue.text: A scholar is a good looker

parts.note: a don is a university teacher and scholar at Oxford or Cambridge

explanation.surface: A clever academic who is also handsome.
explanation.walkthrough: Adonis, in Greek myth a youth of great beauty, now stands for any handsome man.
explanation.definitionFit: The name of the beautiful youth loved by Aphrodite is used for any very attractive man.

clue.text: Some mean narrow-minded girl

indicators.note: Some says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A spiteful, bigoted young woman.
explanation.definitionFit: A female first name stands for a girl in crosswords.

clue.text: Say Rosemary never leaves off

parts.note: read as a plant, rosemary is an example of a shrub that keeps its foliage all year round

explanation.surface: Someone called Rosemary keeps on talking and never stops.
explanation.walkthrough: Rosemary looks like a woman's name and 'leaves off' like stopping; really it is the herb, which never sheds its leaves.
explanation.definitionFit: A plant keeping its foliage through every season is so described, and the herb rosemary is one.

clue.text: Follow directions-and then use incorrectly

parts.note: E and N, east and north, are compass directions

indicators.note: incorrectly says the letters of use are put in the wrong order

explanation.surface: Follow the instructions, then misuse the device anyway.
explanation.walkthrough: 'directions' looks like instructions, but it gives compass points.
explanation.definitionFit: To come after as a result is to follow on, a verb.

clue.text: Trouble in Corfu's soon dealt with

indicators.note: in tells us the answer lies inside the run of words Corfu's soon

explanation.surface: Some bother on a Greek island holiday is quickly sorted out.
explanation.definitionFit: Bother or commotion over a small matter is a trouble, a noun.

clue.text: Confident a Parisian remains inside abed

parts.note: un is French for 'a', as a Parisian would say it

indicators.note: inside says one piece goes within the letters of abed

parts.note: ash is what remains after burning

explanation.surface: A self-assured French person stays put in bed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'remains' looks like a verb (stays) but is a noun, giving ASH.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone not at all embarrassed or ashamed is self-assured.

clue.text: A scene about bottle-opener being missing

parts.note: the opener, or first letter, of bottle is B

indicators.note: about here signals the letters of scene are moved around

explanation.surface: A scene where someone fumbles for a bottle-opener that has gone missing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bottle-opener' is not a corkscrew but the opening letter of bottle; 'about' signals rearranging the letters of scene.
explanation.definitionFit: The state of not being present is a lack or non-attendance, a noun.

clue.text: It may sound useful wear, but it's a hindrance

indicators.note: may sound says the words are heard, not spelt

parts.note: a handy cap is a practical piece of headgear

explanation.surface: A hat that seems practical actually gets in the way.
explanation.definitionFit: A disadvantage or impediment is a hindrance, as in a golfer's or a racehorse's burden.

clue.text: Gathering round about a friend

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so the round thing goes around the friend

parts.note: a ring is a round shape
an ally is a friend or supporter

explanation.surface: Getting together surrounding a companion.
explanation.definitionFit: A mass meeting or coming together, as at a political rally, is a gathering.

clue.text: Obdurate mother interrupting a social worker

indicators.note: interrupting means breaking into, so one piece goes inside the other

parts.note: an ant is a social insect and a worker
a dam is an animal's mother

explanation.surface: A stubborn mum barges in on a welfare officer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'social worker' suggests a welfare officer, but it is the insect ANT.
explanation.definitionFit: Stubborn and unyielding, refusing to change one's mind, are the two adjectives' shared sense.

clue.text: Draws boats

explanation.surface: A sketch of boats.
explanation.definitionFit: To pull hard is a verb sense of draws; small powerful vessels that tow ships are also named this.

clue.text: Many a road may be used for playing games

parts.note: C is the Roman numeral for a hundred, i.e. many

explanation.surface: Many a street may serve as a children's playground.
explanation.walkthrough: The road and games suggest street play; the definition is the pack's playing piece.
explanation.definitionFit: A single piece from a pack is what players hold in bridge or poker.

clue.text: Study opening for dedicated women

parts.note: to con is an old word meaning to study or learn by heart
a vent is an opening for air

explanation.surface: A study room with a window opening for women devoted to their work.
explanation.walkthrough: 'dedicated women' are nuns, who live in this kind of house.
explanation.definitionFit: A community or house of nuns, women devoted to religion, takes this name.

clue.text: An expedition afar is to be organised

indicators.note: to be organised means put in order, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A distant trip has to be planned.
explanation.definitionFit: A journey to observe or hunt wild animals in Africa is an expedition.

clue.text: The experienced sailor goes aloft without publicity

indicators.note: without means outside, so the reversed word surrounds the other piece
in a down clue aloft means going upward, so the word is read bottom to top

parts.note: an ad is a piece of publicity

explanation.surface: A veteran mariner climbs the rigging without any fanfare.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down clue 'aloft' signals reading upward, and 'without' is used in its old sense of outside, not lacking.
explanation.definitionFit: An old salt with long years at sea is called this.

clue.text: She was not in good health on retirement

indicators.note: retiring is withdrawing, going back, so the word is read backwards

parts.note: ailed means was ill

explanation.surface: A woman was poorly after she stopped working.
explanation.walkthrough: 'retirement' suggests leaving work; it signals a reversal.
explanation.definitionFit: A woman's first name stands for any female person in crosswords.

clue.text: American military man mixing general a drink

parts.note: a GI is a US soldier

indicators.note: mixing says the letters of general are stirred up

explanation.surface: A US soldier mixes a cocktail for the general.
explanation.walkthrough: GI is the standard name for an American soldier; 'mixing' signals the rearrangement of general, and the drink is a soft one, not a cocktail.
explanation.definitionFit: A fizzy ginger-flavoured soft drink, often a mixer, is a drink.

clue.text: Bush senior

explanation.surface: George Bush the father, the older president.
explanation.definitionFit: A shrub bearing white flowers and dark berries is one sense; an older person is the other.

clue.text: Twin Greek characters, affectedly stylish

indicators.note: twin says the piece comes as a pair

parts.note: chi is a letter of the Greek alphabet

explanation.surface: Two Greek letters look pretentiously fashionable.
explanation.definitionFit: Showily pretentious, fussily elegant: the word describes chic overdone.

clue.text: An outstanding feature of the seaside

definitions.text: An outstanding feature of the seaside

parts.words: An outstanding feature of the seaside
parts.note: outstanding is read literally as sticking out, a stretch of coast jutting into the sea

explanation.surface: A notable attraction found at the beach.
explanation.walkthrough: 'outstanding' looks like praise, but it means projecting into the water.
explanation.definitionFit: A promontory, a point of coast jutting out into the sea, literally stands out.

clue.text: A deity in state temple

indicators.note: in says one piece goes inside the other

parts.note: PA is the abbreviation for Pennsylvania, a US state
a god is a deity, giving A plus GOD

explanation.surface: A god housed in a national shrine.
explanation.definitionFit: A tiered tower used as a Buddhist or Hindu shrine is a kind of temple.

clue.text: Looking round the civic centre feeling famished

indicators.note: round says one piece goes around the other

parts.note: staring is looking fixedly

indicators.note: centre picks the middle letter of the word civic

explanation.surface: Gazing around the town centre while hungry.
explanation.walkthrough: 'civic centre' looks like a town hall; it is the middle letter V of 'civic'.
explanation.definitionFit: Extremely hungry, ravenous, is the colloquial sense.
